verses.text: In those days Hezekiah became sick and was about to die. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, "This is what the LORD says: 'Put your house in order, because you are going to die. You will not get better.'"
Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD.
He said, "LORD, please remember how I have walked before you faithfully and with all my heart, and have done what is good in your eyes." And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah:
"Go and tell Hezekiah, 'This is what the LORD, the God of your ancestor David, says: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. Look, I will add fifteen years to your life.
I will rescue you and this city from the king of Assyria. I will defend this city.
This is the sign from the LORD to show you that he will do what he has promised:
Look, I will make the shadow cast by the sun go back ten steps on the stairway of Ahaz.'" So the sunlight went back the ten steps it had gone down.
This is what Hezekiah king of Judah wrote after he had been sick and had gotten better:
I said, "In the prime of my life must I go through the gates of the grave? Am I robbed of the rest of my years?"
I said, "I will never again see the LORD, the LORD, in the land of the living. I will no longer look on people or be with those who live in this world.
My home has been pulled down and taken from me like a shepherd's tent. I have rolled up my life like a weaver rolls up cloth. He cuts me off from the loom. From day to night you make an end of me.
I waited patiently until morning, but like a lion he broke all my bones. From day to night you make an end of me.
I cried like a swallow or a crane. I moaned like a dove. My eyes grew tired from looking up to heaven. Lord, I am in trouble. Come and help me!"
But what can I say? He has spoken to me, and he himself has done this. I will walk humbly all my years because of the bitterness of my soul.
Lord, by such things people live, and my spirit finds life in them too. You have healed me and let me live.
Surely it was for my good that I went through such bitter pain. In your love you kept me from the pit of destruction. You have thrown all my sins behind your back.
For the grave cannot praise you. Death cannot sing your praise. Those who go down to the pit cannot hope for your faithfulness.
The living, only the living, can praise you, as I am doing today. Parents tell their children about your faithfulness.
The LORD will save me. So we will sing my songs with stringed instruments all the days of our lives in the house of the LORD.
Isaiah had said, "Prepare a paste of figs and put it on the boil, and he will get better."
Hezekiah had asked, "What will be the sign that I will go up to the house of the LORD?"
